annotation.speech2: The x y plane with a green ellipse centered at the origin and several hyperbolas that are level curves of f equals x y. The red hyperbolas x y equals 2 and x y equals negative 2 are tangent to the ellipse at the four points 2 comma 1, negative 2 comma negative 1, negative 2 comma 1, and 2 comma negative 1. At each of the four points a red arrow shows the gradient of f and a green arrow shows the gradient of g, and in every case the two arrows are collinear. At the two maximum points, 2 comma 1 and negative 2 comma negative 1, they point in the same direction, so lambda is positive; at the two minimum points, negative 2 comma 1 and 2 comma negative 1, they point in opposite directions, so lambda is negative.
The constraint ellipse, x squared over 8 plus y squared over 2 equals 1, drawn in green.
The branch of the level curve x y equals 2 in the first quadrant, drawn in red, tangent to the ellipse at the point 2 comma 1, where f attains its maximum value 2.
The branch of the level curve x y equals 2 in the third quadrant, drawn in red, tangent to the ellipse at the point negative 2 comma negative 1, where f also attains its maximum value 2.
The branch of the level curve x y equals negative 2 in the second quadrant, drawn in red, tangent to the ellipse at negative 2 comma 1, where f attains its minimum value negative 2.
The branch of the level curve x y equals negative 2 in the fourth quadrant, drawn in red, tangent to the ellipse at 2 comma negative 1, where f also attains its minimum value negative 2.
The level curves x y equals 1 and x y equals negative 1, drawn in gray, which cross the ellipse instead of being tangent to it: the values 1 and negative 1 are attained but are not extreme values.
The point 2 comma 1, where the absolute maximum value 2 is attained.
The gradient of f at the point 2 comma 1, drawn in red: it equals i plus 2 j.

The gradient of g at the point 2 comma 1, drawn in green: it equals one half i plus j, so the gradient of f is exactly twice the gradient of g, and lambda equals 2. The two arrows are drawn slightly apart so both are visible.
The gradient of f at the point negative 2 comma negative 1, drawn in red: it equals negative i minus 2 j.

The gradient of g at the point negative 2 comma negative 1, drawn in green: it equals negative one half i minus j, so again the gradient of f is twice the gradient of g and lambda equals 2. The two arrows point the same way and are drawn slightly apart so both are visible.
The gradient of f at the point negative 2 comma 1, drawn in red: it equals i minus 2 j, pointing into the ellipse.

The gradient of g at the point negative 2 comma 1, drawn in green: it equals negative one half i plus j, pointing out of the ellipse. The two arrows lie along the same line but point in opposite directions, so the gradient of f is negative 2 times the gradient of g and lambda equals negative 2.
The gradient of f at the point 2 comma negative 1, drawn in red: it equals negative i plus 2 j, pointing into the ellipse.

The gradient of g at the point 2 comma negative 1, drawn in green: it equals one half i minus j, pointing out of the ellipse. Here too the two gradients are collinear and opposite, so lambda equals negative 2.
